To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ADI vCPC and TSI 3775 nano enhancer are both capable of detecting sub 3 nm particles with detection efficiencies of 50 % or more for 1.4 and 1.8 nm particles, respectively, and with the B3010 the detection efficiencies for 1.8 and 2.5 nm particles were 50 % and 80 %, respectively.

all three CPCs can detect 3 nm particles with high detection efficiencies, that the detection efficiencies are comparable for all CPCs and that the detection efficiencies of all three CPCs are not affected by the particle concentration.

all three instruments are able to detect particles in the 1–3 nm range, but the 3777 is the most sensitive instrument for sub-2 nm particles, the vWCPC is the most sensitive for particles in the 2–4 nm range, and the B3010 is the most sensitive in the 3–6 nm range.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of the three new CPCs and their performance in the sub-3 nm range.
the characterization and intercomparison of the performance of the three newly developed CPCs.
the performance evaluation of the 377, vWCPC and B3010 CPCs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
all three instruments are suitable to detect particles smaller 3 nm, but with different sensitivities.
all three CPCs can be used to detect particles in the sub-3 nm size range, but with varying performance.
the three new CPCs, the ADI vCPC, TSI 3017 and B3010, are able to detect particles as small as 1.3 nm, 1.5 nm, and 2.5 nm in diameter, respectively.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
all three CPCs are capable to detect particles down to 1.3 nm in diameter.

the 3777, vWCPC and B3010 are all able to detect 2 nm diameter particles, but that the 3776 and vWCPC can also measure particles as small as 1 nm in diameter, and that the 37777 and vWCPC are the most suitable for measurements in the sub-2 nm size range.
the ADI versatile WCPC and TSI 3770 nano enhancer have comparable sensitivities and d50s for charged and neutral test particles in the size range of 1–3 nm.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 3777 is a robust, versatile and reliable CPC which can detect particles smaller than d50 = 2.4 ± 0.2 nm.
the 3777 can be used as a reliable sub-3 nm CPC with a d50 of 3.3–3.4 nm for the tungsten test particles.
the 3777 is able to detect sub-3 nm particles with a d50 in the range of ∼1.3 nm at a temperature setting of 20 °C and a d50 in ∼3 nm at 35 °C.
